known_facts_book1: The girl Ruler of the Land of Oz, born of a long line of Fairy Queens and noted for her wisdom as well as her beauty and generosity.
Never leaves her palace in this book; she watches the whole Jinxland adventure in her Magic Picture, which shows any absent person and their surroundings.
Recognizes the Ork on sight when the girls do not, and worries that harm to the strangers would reflect on her because Jinxland is a part of her dominions.
Is relieved when the picture shows the Scarecrow crossing into Jinxland, knowing at once that Glinda has sent him.
Remarks approvingly that Cap'n Bill has never once grumbled over being a grasshopper, as so many would have done.
Has the Wizard place a fully furnished magic house, with supper and beds, in the uninhabited part of the Quadling Country where the Orks land the travellers.
Notices the Scarecrow's accident at the waterfall in the Magic Picture and has the Wizard leave fresh straw beside the house.
Sends Dorothy and Betsy in the Red Wagon to meet the strangers at Glinda's palace, but cannot go herself because of a conference with Jack Pumpkinhead and Professor Wogglebug.
Gives a grand banquet and reception for the new arrivals and closes the book by saying that if Button-Bright is not lost occasionally, he is not happy.

known_facts_book1: A little Kansas girl who came to the Land of Oz in a very curious manner and was made a Princess, living in Ozma's palace as her best friend.
Is loved better than anyone in all Oz next to Ozma, being simple and sweet with a friendly, chummy way.
Brought the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion to the Emerald City, and introduced Ozma to the Shaggy Man, the Hungry Tiger, Billina and Eureka.
Watches the Jinxland adventures with Ozma and Betsy in the Magic Picture, day after day, treating it like a story.
Calls Trot a regular trump while watching her, and asks to go and meet her so she will not feel shy.
Drives to Glinda's palace with Betsy in Ozma's Red Wagon, drawn by the Sawhorse.
Is no fairy but as mortal as anyone, and is sometimes obstinate and gets herself into trouble.

known_facts_book1: Another little girl from the outside world whose strange adventures brought her to the Emerald City, where Ozma welcomed her.
Is a shy little thing who can never get used to the marvels that surround her, and is a firm friend of Dorothy.
Has never met Button-Bright and has to ask who he is when Dorothy spots him in the Magic Picture.
Corrects Dorothy that Cap'n Bill is not one-legged but has one wooden leg.
Rides with Dorothy in the Red Wagon to Glinda's palace to meet the strangers.
Owns a mule named Hank, who is among the animals at Ozma's reception, and tells Trot what the Woozy is.
Appears only in the last four chapters and takes no part in the Jinxland adventure.

known_facts_book1: A quaint little man who inhabits the royal palace and attends to all the magical things Ozma wants done.
Is not as powerful as Glinda, who taught him all the real magic he knows, but can do a great many wonderful things.
Made the Scarecrow's brains, which the Scarecrow calls the Carefully-Assorted, Double-Distilled, High-Efficiency sort and the best the Wizard ever manufactured.

Places a fully furnished magic house — supper smoking hot, three beds, a gold frame reading WELCOME — in the uninhabited Quadling Country for the travellers, and moves it to a new place the following night.
Causes a loaded table to rise out of the ground when Trot says she is hungry on the road.
Leaves a heap of clean crisp straw beside the house so the Scarecrow can be restuffed.
Owns nine tiny piglets, which are among the animals at Ozma's reception.
Comes to the reception late and introduces himself to Trot and Cap'n Bill with 'I know you, but you don't know me; so let's get acquainted.'

known_facts_book1: Ozma's favorite steed, a wooden horse that draws the Red Wagon — a chariot inlaid with rubies and pearls.
Carries Dorothy and Betsy to Glinda's palace and the whole party on to the Emerald City.
Declines to be unharnessed and visit, preferring to stand and think, saying thinking does not bore him at all.
When asked what he will think of, answers: of the acorn that grew the tree from which he was made.
Good-naturedly permits Button-Bright to throw his arms around his neck, recognizing an old friend.
